text: Joe Nzingo Gqabi OLS (6 April 1929 – 31 July 1981) was a South African African National Congress (ANC) activist who served as the ANC's chief representative in Zimbabwe at the time of his assassination by the South African Defence Force in Harare (then Salisbury), Zimbabwe, in 1981. Born on 6 April 1929 in Aliwal North, which is now part of the Joe Gqabi District Municipality, Gqabi's first language was Xhosa. In the 1950s, he worked as a journalist for New Age and maintained frequent contact with ANC leader Walter Sisulu. As a member of the South African Communist Party and UMkhonto we Sizwe, he was sent for guerrilla training in China in the early 1960s. He was captured along with 28 other members undergoing military training in Rhodesia and deported to South Africa, where he was sentenced to two years' imprisonment for illegally leaving the country and ten years under the Sabotage Act, leading to his incarceration at Robben Island. After his release in 1975, he rejoined the ANC. In 1976, he became co-chairman, alongside Martin Ramokgadi, of the clandestine ANC organisation in Johannesburg known as the Main Machinery. During this period, the South African security services attempted to assassinate him by placing a bomb in his car, which was discovered before detonation. He was arrested following the Soweto uprising, where Oliver Tambo later stated he acted as an intermediary between the ANC and the South African Students' Movement, but the police, lacking sufficient evidence, could not build a case against him. He was released in 1977, fled to Botswana, and then moved to Zimbabwe after its independence in 1980. On 31 July 1981, he was assassinated by the South African Defence Force in Ashdown Park, Salisbury (now Harare), Zimbabwe. His body was repatriated to South Africa in 2004 and he was reburied in Aliwal North on 16 December 2004. Posthumously, he was awarded the Order of Luthuli in silver by the South African government, and the Joe Gqabi District Municipality was named in his honour.
